title: deployment.rollback reaches the shared runtime contract and all four digest mirrors
description:
SPIDR prerequisite of task-95e68a8dd2464e7b8ad4b1f8c4d2b2e4, cut by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-05 on the INTERFACE axis. That row asked for scheduled backups, a NEW human-only command kind with "the full roster backfill and a bidirectional set-equality roster test", AND the rollback effect - three deliverables of which the middle one is, on this board, a measured multi-row job on its own.

MEASURED AT HEAD f3b94eaa (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-b63fabf3:
- `git grep -c "deployment\.rollback" -- apps packages` = ZERO. Brand new kind, nothing to duplicate.
- `deployment.deploy` and `deployment.set_target` ARE already on the roster (runtime-vocabulary.ts:91), landed by task-04b3ce7e's contract half - so this row follows a trail its sibling just cut, and should read that row's completionSummary before starting.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the string `deployment.rollback` published on RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, the hand-transcribed EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS and size literal in runtime-contract.test.ts moved with it, the client REGENERATED, and all four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors rotated. Six files, no more.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW AND NOT A CLAUSE: adding ANY kind to RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS rotates the contract digest by construction - contract-digest.ts puts `commandKinds: sortedCopy(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS)` inside canonicalContractSurface(), which deriveContractDigest() SHA256s. There are FOUR mirrors and two of them live under apps/control-room, invisible to `pnpm test` (the root vitest include has no apps/**), `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. A forgotten mirror ships two hard-throwing tests behind three green gates. That trap has already blocked one row on this board.

CENSUS THE MIRRORS YOURSELF with a full-tree `git grep` of the digest literal across ALL file types - the set has moved twice and a `--include=*.ts` grep misses the .tsx one.

NOT IN SCOPE: the daemon vocabulary, families, registry, roster tests, the MCP fence and HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS - all the successor row. The backups and the rollback effect - task-95e68a8d and its successor.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (the only leg that sees mirrors 3 and 4); also run `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm typecheck` and root `pnpm test`, quoting every count line.
definitionOfDone: `deployment.rollback` is a member of RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts in SORTED position, and packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts agrees in BOTH coupled assertions: the hand-transcribed EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS list and the `commands.size` literal. Do NOT derive the expected list from the tuple - that file's own comment forbids it and a derived list asserts nothing. Do NOT freeze the count from this description: run the leg and reconcile against the PRINTED expected/received, because sibling rows move the same literal.

The generated client was REGENERATED, never hand-edited - `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` - with the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST both quoted in the completion record. An UNCHANGED digest means the generator did not see the new kind: that is a stop, not a pass. contract-digest.test.ts DERIVES the digest rather than pinning it, so it must go green WITHOUT being edited.

The mirror set was CENSUSED rather than quoted from this row: `git grep -n <old digest> -- . ':!.moe' ':!pnpm-lock.yaml'` run BEFORE the change (expect four hits) and AFTER (expect zero), across ALL file types. Every hit carries the new hex, including GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 beside CONTRACT_DIGEST in generated-coverage.test.ts. A fifth hit, or a hit in a file type a *.ts grep would miss, is a stop-and-report.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: revert ONLY the apps/control-room mirror and confirm `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` goes RED with the compat gate's own refusal message. That drill is this row's most valuable artifact - it is the only proof the two apps/control-room mirrors are covered by any gate at all.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (MANDATORY), `pnpm typecheck`, and root `pnpm test` - stating plainly that the root lane covers NO apps/** file.
The diff touches exactly six files and no seventh, and ZERO files under apps/daemon/. Prove it with `git status --porcelain -- apps/ packages/` in the completion record.
taskRails: CONTRACT SURFACE ONLY. This row publishes a string on a roster and carries through the digest consequences. It wires no daemon command, defines no refusal code, fences no principal and renders no UI.
NEVER hand-edit the generated client. It is generator output; the only legal way to change it is `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`.
THE DIGEST MIRROR SET MOVES. Census it with a full-tree `git grep` of the LITERAL across all file types before trusting any list, including this row's.
`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` IS MANDATORY: two mirrors live under apps/control-room and no other gate sees them.

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE EVERYTHING NUMERIC. Every literal in this row's description is stale by design — sibling contract rows move the same six files, and three values had ALREADY moved between this row's filing and this plan (2026-09-05):
  - `commands.size` is now 110 at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts:108
  - the digest is now `f07b77e49025d5fd8a6bd391f5848f24103390d23e4db11523346b87f0891bfd`
  - the generated digest line moved to generated-client.ts:919
Also confirmed: task-04b3ce7e's contract half LANDED — runtime-vocabulary.ts:91 now reads `"deployment.deploy", "deployment.set_target", "effect.activate"`. Read that row's completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings; you are following a trail it just cut.

Run and print each:
  (a) `grep -rn 'deployment\.rollback' packages apps --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` — must be EMPTY. If a sibling published it first, STOP and report rather than double-adding.
  (b) `grep -n 'commands.size' packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts` — read the CURRENT literal.
  (c) THE CENSUS, by hex across ALL file types (rail 3):
        D=$(grep -o '"[0-9a-f]\{64\}"' packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts | head -1 | tr -d '"'); echo "$D"
        git grep -n "$D" -- . ':!.moe' ':!.serena' ':!pnpm-lock.yaml'
      Expect FOUR hits: generated-client.ts:919, generated-coverage.test.ts:36, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18, apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255. A `--include=*.ts` grep would miss the .tsx one, and a `git grep GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` would find only one of the four — three hard-code the hex and never name the symbol. A FIFTH hit is a stop-and-report.

Record the OLD digest now; step 3 quotes OLD -> NEW.

THE ROSTER EDIT — two files, both by hand, both at the SORTED position.

POSITION, verified by running an actual sort rather than by eye: `deployment.deploy` < `deployment.rollback` < `deployment.set_target`. So `deployment.rollback` goes BETWEEN the two deployment kinds that already exist, not after them and not beside `effect.activate`. At plan time that neighbourhood is runtime-vocabulary.ts:91.

(1) packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts — insert the kind there.
(2) packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts — the hand-transcribed `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS` carries the same neighbourhood; insert it in the same slot, and move the `expect(commands.size).toBe(N)` literal by exactly ONE. DO NOT derive the expected list from the tuple: the file's header (:29-34) records that an expectation computed from the tuple under test can never fail, which is what the previous `commands.size === RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.length` arm did.

WHICH ARM CATCHES A WRONG SLOT, and it is not the obvious one. `expect(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS).toEqual(EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS)` compares the tuple to a HAND TRANSCRIPTION, so a wrong slot copied consistently into BOTH files stays GREEN. Only the separate "keeps every command kind at its sorted position" arm — which sorts the PRODUCTION tuple and diffs it — can see it. Its docblock records the incident that motivated it: `product_contract.approve_gate_1` once landed between `profile.register` and `project.activate` with both files agreeing on the mistake. Read the failing output rather than guessing.

Run `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test` now for a fast signal before regenerating.

REGENERATE, THEN ROTATE **TWO** HASHES — and only ONE of them is findable by the census. This is the step where this row differs from its siblings, so read it fully.

(1) REGENERATE, never hand-edit (rail 2): `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`. Quote the command, then the OLD digest from step 1 and the NEW one. AN UNCHANGED DIGEST IS A STOP, NOT A PASS (DoD 2) — it means the generator never saw the new kind, because `contract-digest.ts` puts `commandKinds: sortedCopy(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS)` inside `canonicalContractSurface()` and SHA256s it, so a real roster change MUST rotate it.

(2) THE SECOND HASH THE CENSUS CANNOT FIND. `packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts` holds TWO golden constants with DIFFERENT values:
      :35  GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 = "9a4bed62e2f4768fb6565c6e7c24e46874a307701bbf5c1a380b2af3aa78daed"
      :36  CONTRACT_DIGEST       = "f07b77e4…"
`GENERATED_FILE_SHA256` is the SHA256 of the generated FILE'S BYTES, asserted at :164 via `createHash("sha256").update(bytes)`. Regenerating changes those bytes, so it MUST move too — but it is a different value from the contract digest, so a census by the contract-digest hex WILL NOT FIND IT. A worker who censuses correctly, updates all four contract-digest mirrors, and stops will red at :164. The file's own docstring at :30-33 says it: regenerate, review the diff, "then update BOTH constants". Take the new file hash from the failing assertion's own output rather than computing it by hand.

(3) UPDATE THE OTHER THREE contract-digest mirrors to the new hex — generated-coverage.test.ts:36, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18, apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255. Change ONLY the hash string in each; `data-adapter.test.ts` may carry unrelated peer dirt, so leave everything else alone.

(4) RE-CENSUS BOTH WAYS (DoD 3): the NEW digest returns the full four-hit list, and `git grep -n "<OLD digest>" -- . ':!.moe' ':!.serena' ':!pnpm-lock.yaml'` returns NOTHING. Quote both. Note that `contract-digest.test.ts` DERIVES the digest rather than pinning it, so it must go green WITHOUT being edited — if it needs an edit, something is wrong with the regeneration, not with that test.

THE MUTATION DRILL — DoD 4 calls it this row's most valuable artifact, and it is: it is the ONLY proof that the two apps/control-room mirrors are covered by any gate at all.

After everything is green, revert ONE apps/control-room mirror to the OLD digest — use `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255`, the `.tsx`, because it is the hit a `*.ts`-only grep misses and therefore the one most likely to be left stale for real. Then run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and QUOTE THE FAILING LINE verbatim, including the gate's own refusal message.

WHILE THAT MIRROR IS STALE, ALSO RUN `pnpm test` AND `pnpm typecheck` AND CONFIRM BOTH STAY GREEN. That contrast is the whole point: it demonstrates rather than asserts that three gates can be green while a hard-throwing test waits under apps/control-room. Quote all three results together — the red and the two greens — because the pair is the evidence, not the red alone.

Restore the mirror and prove it: all six files here are TRACKED, so an empty `git diff -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx` is a valid restore proof — run it in a call SEPARATE from the restore (global rail 13), and `git status --porcelain` the path BEFORE drilling so you know its pre-drill state.

GATES AND CLOSE.

Run each STANDALONE and FOREGROUND — no pipe, no `;` chain, no `&&` (a piped run reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's):
  1. `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`
  2. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`
  3. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`  — MANDATORY (rail 4). Two mirrors live under apps/control-room and NO other gate sees them: the root vitest include has no `apps/**`, and a stale hex is a string literal so typecheck cannot see it either.
  4. `pnpm typecheck`
  5. `pnpm test` — the root lane. State plainly that it covers NO `apps/**` file, so its count line is not evidence for mirrors 3 and 4.

READ THE OUTPUT, NOT THE EXIT CODE: `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 when the filter misses; "No test files found" and "0 passed" are also exit 0. The discriminator is `Test Files N passed` with N nonzero — quote it for every leg.

Name `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` as the complete_task verification command: it is the only leg that sees the mirrors this row is most likely to get wrong.

If the contracts suite reds on the count, DO NOT edit the number to match this plan — re-read the PRINTED expected-vs-received and take it as authoritative. A sibling row publishing another kind while you worked is expected on these six files, not a conflict.

COMPLETION RECORD states (DoD 6): `git status --porcelain -- apps/ packages/` showing EXACTLY six files and ZERO under apps/daemon/; the generator command with OLD -> NEW contract digest; the OLD and NEW `GENERATED_FILE_SHA256`, called out as a SECOND hash the digest census cannot find; both censuses (new digest = four hits, old digest = zero); the count literal found and the value moved to; and the drill's quoted red alongside the two greens that ran at the same time.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
DECLARING dependsOn ON THE SIBLING CONTRACT ROWS — rejected again, for the reason the last one proved out: the contention on these six files is over LITERALS THAT ARE RE-MEASURED AT CLAIM, not over structure. Between planning task-44760ed1 and planning this row, the count moved 106 -> 110 and the digest rotated twice, and both rows absorb that by reading the printed expected-vs-received. Serialising every kind-publishing row would deadlock a lane that is working correctly.

WHICH MIRROR TO USE FOR THE DRILL — chosen deliberately as `approve-plan.test.tsx`, the `.tsx`. It is the hit a `*.ts`-only grep misses, so it is the one most likely to be left stale in real life, and it lives under apps/control-room where only the mandatory leg can see it. Drilling the `.ts` mirror would prove less.

RUNNING `pnpm test` AND `pnpm typecheck` DURING THE DRILL — added beyond the DoD. DoD 4 asks only for the red. Quoting the red ALONGSIDE two greens taken while the mirror is stale is what turns "the control-room leg is mandatory" from an assertion into a demonstration, and it costs two commands.

TAKING THE NEW FILE HASH FROM THE FAILING ASSERTION rather than computing it by hand — the assertion prints the received value, and hand-computing a SHA256 over a file whose line endings may differ is an avoidable way to get it wrong.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE SECOND HASH THE CENSUS CANNOT FIND. `GENERATED_FILE_SHA256` is a different value from the contract digest, so a correct census plus correct mirror rotation still reds at generated-coverage.test.ts:164. This is the most likely way this row stalls, and the row's own description mentions it only as a sub-clause of DoD 3.

2. A WRONG SORT SLOT COPIED CONSISTENTLY. `deployment.rollback` belongs BETWEEN the two existing deployment kinds; putting it after both, or beside `effect.activate`, is the natural guess. Copied into both files it leaves `toEqual` green and only the sortedness arm red — and one red arm reads like a broken test rather than a real defect.

3. A STALE MIRROR SHIPPING BEHIND GREEN GATES. Two mirrors live under apps/control-room, which the root vitest lane does not cover and typecheck cannot see (a stale hex is a string literal). `pnpm test` + `pnpm typecheck` can both be green with two hard-throwing tests waiting — the drill demonstrates exactly this.

4. CENSUS BY SYMBOL. `git grep GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` finds ONE of the four mirrors and none of the three that matter; a `*.ts` glob silently drops the `.tsx`. The plan pins the hex census in steps 1 and 3 and adds an old-digest census that must return empty.

5. A COUNT FROZEN FROM A DOCUMENT. 110 was true at plan time and will not be if a sibling publishes first. Take the printed expected-vs-received.

6. AN UNCHANGED DIGEST READ AS SUCCESS. It is the signature of a roster edit that never reached `canonicalContractSurface()` — a silent no-op leaving the client without the kind while every mirror still agrees with itself.

7. HAND-EDITING THE GENERATED CLIENT to make a hash line up. Rail 2 forbids it; quoting OLD -> NEW makes a skipped regeneration visible.

8. SCOPE LEAK INTO THE DAEMON. Publishing a string invites wiring it; the daemon vocabulary, registry, MCP fence and HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS are the successor row. DoD 6 wants `git status --porcelain` proving six files and zero under apps/daemon/.
